audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Cassiopeia five of seven stages and the tldr called it a 'free DPS lane', against a 43.21% win rate over 81 games and prose on the same entry reading 'you are not out-poking this lane, you are surviving it' and 'This is where it gets ugly'.
audit.why: Lane difficulty is a key point and this was the single most misleading thing on the page — it told a player they win a lane they lose by seven points.
audit.corrected: Tahm Kench / Skill / Skill / Tahm Kench / Cassiopeia / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench in both layers, with Level 6 the one stage Cassiopeia takes. tldr and winCon rewritten to match. This agrees with the already-audited mirror audits/top/tahmkench__cassiopeia.json, which also has Tahm Kench taking four of seven.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers. The entry says to all-in 'while Abyssal Dive is down' and to commit at 6 without ever stating either duration.
audit.why: Power spikes is a key point and Level 6 is the only stage you win here — the window has to be numbered to be usable.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive 21s at rank 1 falling to 17s, and Miasma's own 24s, quoted in the level-6 spike and the cooldown text. The mirror uses the same 24s figure for Miasma.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. First, the entry says to stun him 'before he can devour himself out of range' and tells you to force out 'that dive and his self-Devour' — Devour targets an enemy or an ally champion, never himself, and it is point-and-click, so Miasma's grounding does not stop it at all. Second, the passive rule is stated as 'three procs of Tongue Lash stun you'; stacks build off any damage he deals, and it is a Tongue Lash landing on a target already at three stacks that stuns and consumes them — three stacks are also what unlock Devour on you.
audit.why: Point 4 is the most important point. A player told that Miasma locks down his ultimate will drop the pool and commit into a Devour; and a player counting only Tongue Lashes will not see the stun or the Devour coming off his autos.
audit.corrected: Miasma grounds Abyssal Dive, his only mobility, and does nothing to Devour; three stacks of An Acquired Taste from any damage arm both the Tongue Lash stun and Devour. This matches the mirror, which independently found the same grounding error on the other side.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (P: 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'; Q: 'If the champion already has 3 stacks... they are stunned'; R: enemy or ally, no self-cast)
champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json (W: 'Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities')

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere, despite the whole entry being about Thick Skin refunding your poke as grey health.
audit.why: Grievous Wounds is what makes the grey-health race winnable; without it every clean Q-E trade nets nothing, which the entry itself admits.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds folded into wants.you[2]. The mirror made the same call from the other side.

edits.before: Poison shreds HP stacking — free DPS lane where only his engage cooldown deserves respect.
edits.after: Grey health eats your poke — this is a survival lane, and level 6 is your only clean window.

edits.before: Out-DPS the HP bar and own the objective fights. Every commit starts with one question: is Abyssal Dive down?
edits.after: Survive to 6, then Miasma his Abyssal Dive and Gaze him. Every commit starts with one question: is Abyssal Dive down?

edits.before: His Q Tongue Lash is a slow skillshot you can sidestep, but landing three procs of his passive (An Acquired Taste) stuns you — never eat a second Tongue Lash while a stack is already on you.
edits.after: Tongue Lash is a slow skillshot you can sidestep. Any damage he deals stacks An Acquired Taste, and a Tongue Lash into three stacks stuns you — three stacks also unlock Devour on you.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze is your one real kill button — land W Miasma first so its grounding locks his W Abyssal Dive in place, then stun him before he can devour himself out of range.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze is your one real kill button — Miasma (24s) grounds Abyssal Dive, his only mobility, then stun him. Grounding does nothing to Devour, which is point-and-click.

edits.before: Tahm Kench stacks raw HP and his R Devour can eat you mid-combo to cancel your Twin Fangs or swallow his own carry out of your poison — your single-target DoT gets out-sustained and out-tanked.
edits.after: Tahm Kench stacks raw HP, and at three stacks Devour eats you mid-combo to cancel the Twin Fang chain or pulls his own carry out of your poison — your DoT is out-sustained and out-tanked.

edits.before: Apply Q poison from max range and chain Twin Fangs, but commit only when his E grey health is already spent and his R Devour is on cooldown
edits.after: Poison from max range and chain Twin Fang, but buy Grievous Wounds early — without it his Thick Skin grey health refunds every trade you win

edits.before: At 4-5 you can chain Twin Fang on a poisoned target, but Tahm Kench just stores it as grey health with E and refunds it by stepping back, then punishes you with a stacked-passive stun if you over-extend to land W. Your only genuine spike is 6: if you land W Miasma to ground his Abyssal Dive escape and then hit Petrifying Gaze, you get a kill before his sustain matters. Force out his W and R first — once that dive and his self-Devour are down, his slow, escape-light body is finally catchable inside your poison.
edits.after: At 4-5 you can chain Twin Fang on a poisoned target, but Tahm Kench stores it as grey health with Thick Skin and refunds it by stepping back, then punishes you with a stacked-passive stun if you over-extend to land W. Your only genuine spike is 6: land Miasma to ground Abyssal Dive, his one piece of mobility, then hit Petrifying Gaze. Grounding never touches Devour, so track the dive's 21s instead — with that spent, his slow, escape-light body is finally catchable inside your poison.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His escape and re-engage — all-in only while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Miasma for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — 21s at rank 1, 17s maxed; all-in only while it is down. - Miasma grounds that blink but never Devour. - Budget W Miasma for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.

notes: Mirror audits/top/tahmkench__cassiopeia.json was already written and I reused its findings rather than re-deriving them; the two sides now agree that Tahm Kench takes four of seven stages, that Miasma grounds Abyssal Dive and not Devour, and that Grievous Wounds is required. full.diff is 'HARD' but diffRating is 4/10 on a 43.21% lane — the rating is the outlier and should be raised; I left it because I could not confirm the field's scale. The mirror flagged the same class of mismatch across this file.
